holidays.name: National Dictionary Day
holidays.description: A day for word nerds, logophiles and anyone who has ever argued over a spelling. Celebrate by learning a new word, settling a debate with a good dictionary, or reading a few pages for fun.
holidays.origin: The day marks the birthday of Noah Webster, born October 16, 1758 in Connecticut. Webster published his landmark American Dictionary of the English Language in 1828, and it helped shape American spelling and usage.
holidays.funFact: Webster's dictionary helped popularize American spellings such as 'color' instead of 'colour' and 'center' instead of 'centre'.

holidays.name: National Boss's Day
holidays.description: A day for employees to thank the person who signs off on their vacation days. Typical gestures include cards, small gifts, a team lunch, or just a sincere thank-you.
holidays.origin: Patricia Bays Haroski registered the observance in the United States. She chose October 16, her father's birthday, and he was her boss. The day is observed on October 16, or the nearest working day.
holidays.funFact: Greeting card companies embraced the day, and Hallmark now sells cards for it.

holidays.name: National Liqueur Day
holidays.description: A toast to sweet, flavorful spirits infused with fruits, herbs, nuts, spices, and creams. Sip one neat, pour it over ice cream, or mix it into a cocktail.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates liqueurs, which were once known as cordials and have a long history in monasteries and apothecaries.
holidays.funFact: Many classic liqueurs began as medicinal tonics, brewed by monks and apothecaries to soothe ailments.
